The fix is at the right layer. Could we avoid the quadratic `filter`/`some` scan by sorting replacements by start position ascending, with the outermost range first when starts are equal, then assembling the result from the original content in a single pass? Ranges covered by an already accepted replacement can be skipped, while independent occurrences of the inner expression should still be replaced.

Please also add coverage for an inner expression used outside the enclosing replacement, and for identical full nested expressions that exercise the subsequent expression-cache pass. Cleaning up unused inner cache declarations can remain a separate follow-up; this fix doesn’t need a broader cache-analysis refactor.

nodes.body: Thanks! `applyContentReplacements` now sorts by start (outermost first on ties) and builds the result in a single pass, skipping ranges covered by an accepted replacement. I also added tests for an inner expression used on its own and for a repeated full nested expression going through the expression-cache pass. Cleaning up unused inner declarations is left for a follow-up.
